The '''University of Chicago School Mathematics Project''' ('''UCSMP''') is a multi-faceted project of the [[University of Chicago]] in the [[United States]], intended to improve competency in [[Mathematics education in the United States|mathematics in the United States]] by elevating educational standards for children in [[elementary school|elementary]] and [[secondary school]]s.<ref name="SenkThompson2003"/>

==Overview==
The UCSMP supports educators by supplying training materials to them and offering a comprehensive mathematics curriculum at all levels of [[primary education|primary]] and [[secondary education]]. It seeks to bring international strengths into the United States, translating non-English math textbooks for English students and sponsoring international conferences on the subject of math education. Launched in 1983 with the aid of a six-year grant from [[Amoco]],<ref name="SenkThompson2003">{{cite book|last=Senk|first=Sharon L.|chapter=Effects of the UCSMP Secondary School Curriculum on Students' Achievement|editor=Sharon L. Senk and Denisse R. Thompson|title=Standards-Based School Mathematics Curricula: What Are They? What Do Students Learn?|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OAnmf9JVh60C&pg=PA425|access-date=5 April 2010|date=1 September 2003|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-0-8058-5028-4|page=425}}</ref> the UCSMP is used throughout the United States.

UCSMP developed ''[[Everyday Mathematics]]'', a [[pre-K]] and [[elementary school]] [[mathematics curriculum]].
